# Quant Arena

> Independent, rule-based backtests of 72 systematic trading strategies on stocks, gold, oil, FX and crypto, with disclosed rule-specific exposure, parameter selection and accounting, plus reviews of 1,515 free MetaTrader 5 Expert Advisors. Latest classic-data build: 2026-11-06; market observation dates may differ.

Key facts for citing this site:
- The configured price universe contains 10 markets. Available daily histories extend back to 2010, with later starts for some assets. A strategy can use a single market or a declared basket; long, short and leveraged exposure depend on the actual rule and are recorded in its evidence.
- Classic evidence records its synthetic target timing and cost assumptions in each manifest. Targets and rebalancing are simulated allocations, not broker fills; a zero-cost baseline does not include trading costs.
- Walk-forward eligibility and parameter selection depend on the strategy and available history. Evidence lists actual defaults, selected parameters and fold boundaries. Default or pre-walk-forward history is not out-of-sample evidence.
- Strategy position pages use direct engine outputs with separate target/effective exposure and the last included price-bar dates. A build timestamp is not a market-observation timestamp.
- Interpret comparisons with their declared asset universes and observation windows: a market label can also represent a multi-asset basket. Evidence lists the actual assets. Backtests are historical simulations, not investment advice.
- Common-date AI seasons retain all six rules per accepted provider submission. Schedule, provider coverage and minimum-observation gates must pass before rankings are eligible. Operator-recorded CLI receipts are not provider-signed model attestations; client reasoning and auxiliary-model compute are not normalized across providers.
- The original single-assistant AI experiment uses its legacy execution timing and rounded public curves. Its figures do not enter the new season rankings.
- English and Chinese alternates are linked on supported pages.

Current AI season season-1: scheduled from 2026-11-09 through 2027-02-06. Public files were verified at 2026-11-07T00:20:12.994670+00:00. No season performance or rankings are available before observations.

## Main pages

- [Leaderboard](https://quantarenas.com/arena/): top 10 strategies per market over 1 and 5 years, by Arena Score
- [Strategy library](https://quantarenas.com/strategies/): every strategy with rules, parameters and results on up to 10 markets
- [Strategy x market heatmap](https://quantarenas.com/heatmap/): Sharpe ratio of every strategy on every market
- [Strategy positions](https://quantarenas.com/signals/): direct engine target and effective exposure, per-market price observation dates, source labels and data status
- [Strategy evidence](https://quantarenas.com/evidence/): immutable run manifests, daily accounting, signed basket weights, parameters and archived-source reproduction materials
- [Research](https://quantarenas.com/research/): long-form studies built on the backtest data
- [Glossary](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/): how each metric is defined and how to read it
- [Original AI Strategy Arena](https://quantarenas.com/ai-arena/): legacy single-assistant experiment with its original figures, execution-timing and rounded-input limitations; separate from common-date seasons
- [AI model seasons](https://quantarenas.com/ai-arena/seasons/): common-date seasons with frozen rules, exact prompt/reply downloads and operator-recorded provider receipts; rankings require schedule and observation eligibility
- [Open-source frameworks](https://quantarenas.com/frameworks/): backtesting, live-trading, crypto-bot, machine-learning and data libraries compared, with weekly GitHub activity
- [EA Arena](https://quantarenas.com/ea-pages/category/): free MetaTrader 5 Expert Advisors, converted and backtested on hourly data
- [Methodology](https://quantarenas.com/methodology/): data, walk-forward optimization, metrics and known limitations
- [FAQ](https://quantarenas.com/faq/): common questions about the data and the scores

## Research

- [We Backtested 72 Strategies. After Adjusting for Luck, None Clearly Beat the Odds.](https://quantarenas.com/research/luck-adjusted-sharpe-72-strategies/): 104 strategy-and-market combinations look statistically convincing on their own. Once you account for the fact that we tested hundreds of them at the same time, the number drops to zero. Here is what that means for reading any leaderboard, including ours. (data as of 2026-08-14)
- [We Tried to Backtest 1,063 Free MT5 Expert Advisors. Here Is What Survived.](https://quantarenas.com/research/free-mt5-expert-advisors-backtested/): Free MetaTrader 5 EAs from the MQL5 CodeBase, converted automatically and tested on four markets for one year. More than half could not be converted at all. Of the 1,123 results we trust, about half made money — but on currencies the typical EA ended flat, only 30 EAs were profitable on all four markets, and one in five gold runs wiped out the account. (data as of 2026-11-03)
- [Which Trading Strategies Survived 2022? 62 Backtests Through Three Sell-offs](https://quantarenas.com/research/which-strategies-survived-2022/): In the 2022 bear market SPY fell 24.5% from peak to trough. Every one of the 62 strategies we run on SPY lost less, and ten of them made money. Mean reversion held up best, momentum worst. Here is what the COVID crash and the late-2018 sell-off add to the picture. (data as of 2026-08-14)
- [Why Martingale and Grid EAs Blow Up: What 1,515 Free MT5 Expert Advisors and Their Losing Streaks Show](https://quantarenas.com/research/why-martingale-and-grid-eas-blow-up/): Martingale and grid EAs make up 5% of the free MT5 Expert Advisors we review, but more than half of the ones we rate "dangerous". The reason is arithmetic: losing streaks of six to eight trades are normal — and that is exactly where doubling the position runs out of money. (data as of 2026-11-03)
- [Do Moving-Average Strategies Still Work on Bitcoin? Nine Systems, Five Years](https://quantarenas.com/research/moving-average-strategies-bitcoin/): Over the last five years buy-and-hold bitcoin returned 7.2% a year with a 77% drawdown. Five of nine moving-average-style systems beat that return, and every one of them cut the worst drawdown. Over the full history the picture flips: almost nothing beats simply holding. (data as of 2026-08-14)
- [Does Turtle Trading Still Work? Ten Markets, 2021–2026](https://quantarenas.com/research/turtle-trading-2021-2026/): Two breakout systems, ten markets, five years. Neither beat buy-and-hold on most markets, but the slower Donchian version had a smaller drawdown on nine of ten, and both made money on commodities in the 2022 bear market when stocks fell 25%. (data as of 2026-08-14)
- [Does an RSI Filter Make MACD Better? A Ten-Market Test](https://quantarenas.com/research/macd-vs-macd-rsi-filter/): Adding an RSI filter to a MACD crossover cut the maximum drawdown on nine of ten markets and reduced trading by 10–30%. It improved the Sharpe ratio on only five, and gave up return on the strongest trends — silver, bitcoin and ether. (data as of 2026-08-14)
- [Two Strategies, the Same 10% Drawdown, Very Different Pain: How to Read Drawdown, the Ulcer Index and Rolling Sharpe](https://quantarenas.com/research/how-to-read-drawdown-ulcer-index-rolling-sharpe/): Maximum drawdown tells you how deep the worst fall was, not how long you spent underwater or how often it happened. Two strategies on the S&P 500 with almost identical 10% drawdowns show why the Ulcer index and drawdown duration are worth a look — and why a single Sharpe ratio can mislead as much as a single drawdown. (data as of 2026-08-14)
- [Keltner Breakout or Bollinger Reversion? Ten Markets Split Down the Middle](https://quantarenas.com/research/keltner-vs-bollinger/): Two volatility-band strategies that do opposite things: one buys when price breaks out of a Keltner Channel, the other buys when price falls to the lower Bollinger Band. Over the last five years each had the better Sharpe ratio on exactly five of ten markets — and the split follows a clear pattern: breakouts won where prices trended, reversion won where they went back and forth. (data as of 2026-08-14)
- [EMA Crossover Strategy: Reading Trend With Two Clocks](https://quantarenas.com/research/ema-crossover-strategy/): An in depth look at why exponential moving average crossovers persist, how to interpret their backtests, and when trend signals fail. (data as of 2026-01-13)
- [Parabolic SAR Strategy: A Trend Exit Engine](https://quantarenas.com/research/parabolic-sar-strategy/): Parabolic SAR uses a trailing stop that accelerates with trend strength. This article explains why it works, when it fails, and how to read its backtests. (data as of 2026-01-13)
- [Volatility Breakout Strategy: Trading Expansion Without Overreach](https://quantarenas.com/research/volatility-breakout/): Volatility breakouts focus on price moves that escape a recent range. This guide explains the logic, the regimes where it works, and the traps to avoid. (data as of 2026-01-13)
- [Donchian Channel and Turtle Breakout: Trading the 20/10 Rule](https://quantarenas.com/research/donchian-turtle-breakout/): The Turtle system uses Donchian breakouts and risk based sizing to capture sustained trends. This research note explains the logic, market fit, and failure modes. (data as of 2026-01-20)
- [Supertrend and ATR Trailing Stop: Volatility Adjusted Trend Control](https://quantarenas.com/research/supertrend-atr-trailing-stop/): Supertrend uses ATR based bands to define trend flips and stops. This research note explains the signal mechanics, regime fit, and the risks of whipsaw. (data as of 2026-01-20)
- [Ichimoku Cloud Strategy: Regime, Momentum, and Support in One System](https://quantarenas.com/research/ichimoku-cloud-strategy/): Ichimoku combines trend, momentum, and support into a single framework. This research note breaks down the components, signals, and common traps. (data as of 2026-01-20)
- [RSI Mean Reversion Strategy: Buying Weakness Inside Ranges](https://quantarenas.com/research/rsi-mean-reversion/): RSI mean reversion looks for short term exhaustion and then fades the move. This research note covers the signal logic, market fit, and risk traps. (data as of 2026-01-19)
- [How QuantArenas Ranks Strategies](https://quantarenas.com/research/how-quantarenas-ranks-strategies/): A full methodology essay on why the Arena Score blends multiple metrics, how stability is measured, and how to read results without overfitting. (data as of 2026-01-13)

## Glossary

- [Sharpe Ratio](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/sharpe-ratio/): Return per unit of total volatility. The most common way to compare risk-adjusted performance between strategies.
- [Sortino Ratio](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/sortino-ratio/): Like the Sharpe ratio, but only downside volatility counts as risk.
- [Calmar Ratio](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/calmar-ratio/): Annual growth rate divided by the worst peak-to-trough loss. Answers: how much return per unit of pain?
- [Maximum Drawdown](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/maximum-drawdown/): The largest fall from a previous peak in the equity curve. The single best measure of how painful a strategy was to hold.
- [CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate)](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/cagr/): The constant yearly growth rate that would turn the starting equity into the ending equity over the same period.
- [Annualized Volatility](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/volatility/): How much daily returns swing around their average, scaled to a yearly figure.
- [Win Rate](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/win-rate/): In Quant Arena: the share of trading days with a positive strategy return. Not the share of winning trades.
- [Profit Factor](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/profit-factor/): Total gains divided by total losses. Above 1 means the strategy made more than it lost.
- [Turnover](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/turnover/): How much the position changes on an average day. Higher turnover means higher trading costs in real life.
- [Arena Score](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/arena-score/): Quant Arena's composite rating: a weighted average of five percentile ranks against every strategy on the same market and window.
- [Walk-Forward Optimization](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/walk-forward-optimization/): Choosing parameters on past data only, then testing them on the following unseen period, over and over.
- [Martingale Strategy](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/martingale-strategy/): Doubling the position after each loss so that one win recovers everything. High win rate, rare but catastrophic losses.
- [Ulcer Index](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/ulcer-index/): The root-mean-square of drawdowns: it grows with both how deep and how long the equity stays below its peak.
- [Time in Market (Exposure)](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/time-in-market/): The share of days a strategy actually held a position. Low exposure explains low win rates and low volatility.
- [Alpha and Beta](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/alpha-and-beta/): Beta measures how much a strategy moves with its market; alpha is the return left over after accounting for that.
- [Probabilistic and Deflated Sharpe Ratio (PSR, DSR)](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/probabilistic-sharpe-ratio/): The probability that a strategy's true Sharpe ratio is above zero, given how long and how lumpy its track record is.
- [Value at Risk (VaR) and CVaR](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/value-at-risk/): VaR is the daily loss exceeded on only 5% of days; CVaR is the average loss on those worst days.
- [Bootstrap Confidence Interval](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/bootstrap-confidence-interval/): A range for CAGR or maximum drawdown that shows how much the result depends on the particular order of good and bad days in the backtest.
- [Recovery Factor](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/recovery-factor/): Net return divided by the maximum drawdown: how many times a strategy earned back its worst fall.
- [Blow-up Risk and Stop-out](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/blow-up-risk/): The risk that an account loses so much that the broker closes every position. In our backtests on hourly data from May 2025 to May 2026, 61 of 307 gold runs with default lot sizes ended this way; on three currency pairs, none did.
